data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Paraguay factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Paraguay performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to 2017. Paraguay participated for the first time in PISA in 2017 under PISA for Development, and in 2022 the assessment was administered as a paper-and-pencil test with a two-hour duration, complemented by a student background questionnaire (~35 minutes) and a school principal questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 baseline and Level 5/6 top performers), and uncertainty via 95% confidence intervals. It also highlights within-country gaps by socioeconomic status (ESCS quintiles), gender differences, and several school-life and COVID-related experience indicators, noting that only 68% of students reached the final COVID-closure section (so those results require caution). No predictive modeling or ML-based estimation is described in the provided text.
